correctness.rationale: Exact face areas and the Cauchy formula yield \(B_c(u)=aS+bD\) for every c and u, including endpoints by continuity. A complete split of the nonnegative unit-normal sphere into balanced/dominant cones gives sharp upper bounds using Cauchy–Schwarz and sharp lower bounds from 3 extreme rays plus the triangle inequality. Equality cases and orbit sizes follow from equality strictness. The ratio b/a is strictly decreasing; its crossings with \(2/3\) and \(\sqrt2-1\) give the two exact algebraic values and all equality transitions. The independent direct convex-hull checker reproduced 5460 shadow areas across the continuum parameter domain, as finite corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Compared full accessible primary descriptions of the exact same cube–octahedron interpolation, including previous full polytope facet-network, tetrahedral volume, and illumination proofs, and the recoverable prior fixed-body brightness claims at \(c=3/2\) and \(c=2\). The new continuum profile identifies two separate interior algebraic parameter transitions with complete global maximizing and minimizing orientation sets; neither fixed-body law gives these transitions, and no inspected full prior result states their inequalities or equality classification. The known facet areas and Cauchy identity are acknowledged inputs, not claimed discoveries. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A differently phrased historical treatment of brightness extrema of a truncated octahedron family could predate this calculation.

The complete text of Burger–Gritzmann (2000) was not available through attempted online searches; its abstract has no indication of this specific family but cannot by itself eliminate broader coverage.
Full original body of Tiwary (2008) was not material-read; its title and abstract concern algorithms and complexity rather than parametric sharp extrema.
Older single-body special cases and generic Cauchy projection formula are known; no novelty is claimed for them.

value.rationale: The exact range of orthographic projection area and every attaining view are fundamental, scale-sensitive, natural geometric invariants of a widely studied cube–octahedron truncation path. Two distinct sharp symmetry-breaking crossings happen strictly within one fixed combinatorial chamber rather than at its obvious cuboctahedral boundary. This gives a complete, nontrivial viewing-direction phase diagram that distinguishes continuous shadow geometry from the known fixed-shape formulas, facet area tables, illumination, and contained-simplex extremals.
